summary: ATR does not pick direction on its own: ATR(14) crossing up through ATR(100) did no better than random candles on 1h, 4h or daily. The result that holds up is in quiet markets, where longs taken while ATR(14) sat below ATR(100) did worse than random on 1h and 4h, even without their strongest stretch. Longs taken while ATR(14) sat above ATR(100) beat random, mostly on SOL, because price moved more after those volatile candles in a window that rose.

verdicts.use: Going long in volatile markets (ATR(14) above ATR(100))
verdicts.text: Beat random entries on 1h and 4h, and on 4h it held at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles. Price moved more after these volatile candles in a window that rose, so this reflects timing rather than direction, and SOL carries most of it.

verdicts.use: Going long in quiet markets (ATR(14) below ATR(100))
verdicts.text: Worse than random on 1h and 4h, and the gap held without its strongest stretch. On 4h the gap came from uptrends; in downtrends it showed nothing.

verdicts.use: Going long on a volatility spike (ATR(14) crossing up ATR(100))
verdicts.text: No better than random entries on 1h, 4h or daily.

verdicts.use: Going long as volatility fades (ATR(14) crossing down ATR(100))
verdicts.text: On 1h it trailed random entries after 20 candles but at no other horizon. On 4h and daily it sat inside the luck band.

verdicts.use: Fast volatility cross (ATR(7) crossing up ATR(28))
verdicts.text: On 1h it beat random by a hair, and the gap vanishes without signals on Feb 3–9, 2021. The cross fires in fast candles in a window that rose, so even that gap is not a pick of direction, and on 4h and daily it showed nothing.

notes: On 4h, longs taken while ATR(14) sat above ATR(100) gave 16,749 entries in 298 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.55% ahead of random entries, above a luck band of -0.45% to 0.42%. The gap shows at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles and holds without its strongest stretch. SOL carries it at 1.33% ahead, while BTC at 0.18% and ETH at 0.19% sat inside their bands.

Read that gap as volatility, not direction. These candles cluster in fast stretches, and the luck band keeps their timing but not their volatility. In a window where price rose, entries in volatile stretches beat random because price moved more after them. On 4h in uptrends the 0.58% gap vanishes without SOL signals between Jul 31 and Sep 24, 2021, and in downtrends the setting was 0.21% behind random, inside the band.

On 1h the same setting was 0.13% ahead after 20 candles. It also led at 10 candles, but not at 50 or 100. SOL led at 0.26% ahead, BTC lost its gap without signals on Jan 2–9, 2021, and ETH sat inside its band. In uptrends and in downtrends alike, the 1h gap vanishes without its strongest stretch.

The quiet reading is the result that holds up. On 4h, longs taken while ATR(14) sat below ATR(100) were 0.39% behind random entries after 20 candles, below a band of -0.30% to 0.32%. They trail at 10, 20, 50 and 100 candles and hold without their strongest stretch. In 4h uptrends the gap was 0.60%, while in downtrends it showed nothing, and on 1h it was 0.10% behind in both regimes.

The crosses carry less. ATR(14) crossing up through ATR(100) sat inside the luck band on 1h, 4h and daily. ATR(7) crossing up ATR(28) on 1h was 0.08% ahead, a gap that vanishes without signals on Feb 3–9, 2021. In 1h downtrends it was 0.13% ahead and in uptrends it showed nothing, but it fires in fast candles, so this reflects bigger moves after it, not a pick of direction.

For a long DCA bot, ATR(14) below ATR(100) on 1h or 4h is a reason to leave entries out. After those quiet stretches, price did worse than random. ATR(14) above ATR(100) says the next moves tend to be larger, which matters for how far you set the take profit and DCA steps, not for direction. The setting breaks in 4h downtrends, where neither level showed anything.
